connections.title: Connections

connections.tokenKeep: Leave it empty to keep the saved token.
connections.removeConfirm.body: Pictures stop going there at once. Jobs that chose it fall back to their default.
connections.google.hint: Lets people log in and sign up with their Google account, over https or on this machine.
connections.google.redirectsHint: In Google Cloud's console: an OAuth client of the type Web application, with these as its authorised redirect URIs.
connections.removeConfirm.googleBody: Nobody can log in with Google until it is set up again. Linked accounts stay linked.
connections.legal.hint: Who runs this Delve, as the public privacy policy and terms show it.

storage.title: Storage
storage.intro: Only the install's owner sees these. A SAS URL or secret key stays in this machine's files: Delve never shows it again, it only says where the store is and whether its secret is set.
ownerToken.title: Owner token
ownerToken.intro: The owner token opens Delve as the owner, with no login, on this machine and its network; over the internet it isn't taken, and you log in with your owner account. If a link with it got out, make a new one: the old token and its links stop working at once.
ownerToken.confirmBody: The old token and every link that carried it stop working at once, on every device that used them.
ownerToken.made: The old token and its links no longer work. Open one of these on each device of yours that used the old one:
ownerToken.once: Shown once. On the machine Delve runs on, uv run delve token prints the links again.
storage.backup.hint: Your own, private: every day Delve copies the modules, campaigns and settings that changed here. Keep its credential to yourself.
storage.library.hint: Shared with friends: the modules you publish, and the ones you download. Its credential decides what this install may do there.
storage.sasUrl.hint: The container's SAS URL. Backups need read, list, create, write and delete.
storage.account.hint: Your Cloudflare account id: the endpoint is https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com.
storage.endpoint.hint: The address alone, starting with https://.
storage.accessKeyId.hint: Type the saved key's id again to keep its secret.
storage.secretSet: Set: leave empty to keep it
storage.writeRight.hint: On R2 the storage can't tell publish from manage; Delve keeps to it, other tools need not.
storage.expiresDay: SAS expires within a day, on {date}
storage.expired: SAS expired on {date}: Delve can't reach this store until you save a new one.
storage.removeConfirm.backup.body: Delve stops backing up. What is in the store stays there.
storage.removeConfirm.library.body: The Library tab goes. Modules you downloaded stay on this install.
storage.time.hint: This machine's time. A backup missed while Delve was off runs when it starts.
storage.run.partial: Partly backed up on {when}: what failed is tried again next time
storage.unused.title: Files nothing uses
storage.unused.intro: Pictures, books and maps stay in the store after what used them is gone or replaced. Look for them to see how much space they take, then delete them. Files from the last day, or from a job still running, stay.
storage.unused.none: Every stored file is in use.
storage.unused.kept: Newer files nothing uses yet, which stay: {count}.
storage.unused.confirm.body: They can't be brought back, except from a copy of the data folder. Delve looks again first, and keeps any that something uses by then.

packs.title: Rulesets and settings
packs.intro: The rulesets and settings installed on this Delve, as packs. Download one to install it on another Delve.
packs.restartNeeded: The packs changed: Delve uses them once it restarts.
packs.restartByHand: Delve can't restart itself here: restart it as you started it.
packs.restarted: Delve restarted and uses the packs as they are now. Reload any open play page.
packs.uploadHint: A .delvepack file. A pack of an id that's installed replaces it.
packs.installBody: A pack holds code that runs on this server when it's installed and whenever Delve starts. Install only packs you trust.
packs.removeBody: Delve stops using it once it restarts. You can install it again from its .delvepack file.
packs.removeInUse: These campaigns use it, and can't be played until it's installed again: {campaigns}.
packs.restartBody: Delve stops for a few seconds and comes back with the packs as they are now; open pages connect again.
packs.restartBeats: The DM is answering at {campaigns}: that beat fails, and its host can try it again.
packs.restartConversion: {title} is being converted: it pauses and goes on, the piece under way done again.

editor.simplify.title: Simplify map
editor.simplify.lede: Removes corridor nodes and room points that don’t change what is drawn. The result goes into the editor — review it, then Save (Ctrl+Z undoes it).
editor.simplify.doorSpurs: Also remove stubs that end at a door
editor.simplify.doorSpursHint: (the map looks the same; the door’s fog-of-war fade then starts at the nearest remaining corridor end)
editor.tool.select.hint: Drag to pan, wheel to zoom. Click a room/corridor to jump to its definition.
editor.tool.rect.hint: Drag from one corner to the opposite.
editor.tool.circle.hint: Drag from the centre outward to set the radius.
editor.tool.polygon.hint: Click each corner; double-click (or Enter) to close. Esc cancels.
editor.tool.cave.hint: Like polygon, but walls render with a natural wavy edge (line_style organic). Click corners; double-click / Enter to close.
editor.tool.corridor.hint: Click waypoints to extend; click an existing node to branch a junction from it. Double-click / Enter finishes, Esc cancels. Snaps to half-cells.
editor.tool.door.hint: Click on a wall to drop a door — the rooms it connects are inferred from position. Set type / state / facing in the toolbar.
editor.tool.feature.hint: Click a cell to drop a feature. Pick the type, rotation and scale in the toolbar.
editor.tool.text.hint: Type the text and pick a size in the toolbar, then click the map to place it at that fixed point.
editor.tool.area.hint: Pick a kind (water, lava, pit…) in the toolbar, then click each corner of the pool/area; double-click or Enter to close, Esc cancels. Not a room.
editor.tool.line.hint: Pick a style (bars, curtain, barred) in the toolbar, then click each point along the line; double-click or Enter to finish, Esc cancels.
editor.tool.exit.hint: Set the destination map + landing position in the toolbar, then click where the exit sits on this map. Stepping on it sends the party to the other map.
editor.snap.hint: Snap coordinates to whole grid units
editor.res.hint: Snap resolution: 1 = one dot per grid edge, 2 = twice as many dots (half-steps), 3 = thirds, …
editor.pathing.hint: Pathing check: rooms/corridors with a door are tinted green, isolated ones red
editor.connections.hint: In Select mode, click a room/corridor to list the doors connecting it
editor.cellGrid.hint: Draw a per-cell grid inside every room and corridor (adds `cell_grid` to the map block)
editor.door.facing: Leaf side (auto = inferred by the renderer)
editor.door.trapped.hint: Mark the door trapped (DM only — hidden from the players' fog-of-war view)
editor.feature.global.hint: Always add the feature as a top-level declaration. When off, a feature dropped on a room/corridor is nested inside it (features on empty space are always global).
editor.corridor.organic.hint: Draw corridors with an organic (wavy, hand-drawn) wall style
editor.corridor.straight.hint: Draw corridors with straight (sharp) corners instead of rounded
editor.text.size: Font size (1 = a default room label)
editor.text.description.hint: What the glyph means — shown as a hover tooltip / map key
editor.text.global.hint: Always add the text as a top-level declaration. When off, text dropped on a room/corridor is nested inside it (text on empty space is always global).
editor.area.organic.hint: Give the area a natural wavy edge (line_style organic)
editor.exit.map: Map this exit leads to (other maps in this module)
editor.exit.x: Landing X on the destination map
editor.exit.y: Landing Y on the destination map
editor.exit.label: Label (optional)
editor.exit.secret.hint: Mark the exit secret (DM only — hidden from the players' fog-of-war view until discovered)
editor.exit.global.hint: Always add the exit as a top-level declaration. When off, an exit dropped on a room/corridor is nested inside it (exits on empty space are always global).
editor.sort.hint: Reorder declarations: rooms (by id), corridors (by id), doors, then features
editor.reference.hint: Load a reference image to trace over (stays in your browser; never saved to the map)

newModule.emptyHint: Start from a title, and write the rest in the module's editor.
newModule.pdfHint: A module's PDF becomes its texts, its NPCs and encounters, its images and its maps, traced from the book's own map pages. The texts keep the book's own words.
newModule.bookMaps: Draw each map from the book's map page
newModule.bookMapsHint: After the conversion, Delve draws each sketched map again from the book's own map, as a draft beside the sketch: keep it or discard it on the module's Maps tab.
newModule.describeHint: For example: a dungeon with kobolds, no plot. It becomes a small module with a sketched map, ready to play. A campaign-sized request is written in steps: an outline, then each level with its own map.
newModule.pictures: Paint pictures of its key people and places
newModule.picturesHint: Claude picks the people and places most worth showing, and each is painted once. The DM shows them to the players as handouts, so they always look the same.
newModule.picturesOwner: Only the owner may paint with a paid image model.
newModule.picturesPaid: Each picture costs money, on the image model chosen for scenes.
newModule.sizingUp: Claude is sizing up your request…
newModule.scopeCampaign: Claude reads this as a campaign: it is written in steps, an outline, then each level with its own map.
newModule.scopeSandbox: Claude reads this as a sandbox: an outline of the region first, then each place with its own floor plan, and a region map drawn from the outline.
newModule.scopeModule: Claude reads this as one module, written in one go.
newModule.scopeHint: Answer what you want to decide, then Generate. A question left empty keeps what Claude assumes.
newModule.oneAtATime: One conversion runs at a time: a book you upload or a module you describe now waits in the queue, and starts by itself when its turn comes.

This campaign is kept as it is and set to complete. Claude then writes the party's history for the new campaign. In the same setting the calendar goes on from today's date and time; in another it starts again.

landing.lede: A tabletop role-playing game in your browser. An AI game master runs the adventure; you and your friends play it, together or in turns, from wherever you are.
landing.inviteOnly: New here? Ask whoever runs this Delve for an invite.
landing.steps: How you get to a table
landing.step.in.text: Open the invite a host sent you, or ask for an account here and wait to be let in.
landing.step.character.text: Roll one up with the game master, or take one of the adventure's ready-made heroes.
landing.step.play.text: Say what your character does. The game master answers, rolls by the rules and moves the story on, and the map shows what your party has seen.
landing.find.dm: A game master who never cancels
landing.find.dm.text: Claude runs the world: describes it, speaks for the people you meet, plays the monsters fairly and keeps to the rules of the game you play.
landing.find.adventures.text: Classic modules turned into adventures to play, with their keyed rooms, maps and treasure.
landing.find.maps: Maps that fill in as you go
landing.find.maps.text: Dungeon and world maps show only what the characters have seen, and a journey between places takes its days.
landing.find.table.text: Play at the same time with voice at the table, take turns at your own pace, or play alone.
landing.find.sheet.text: Hit points, spells, gear and experience follow what happens in play.
landing.find.settings.text: Aun, Delve's own world, and the others your Delve has installed, with their lore, their calendars and their maps.
landing.private: Delve is private: it runs on its owner's computer, for the people they let in.

sheet.savesExplain: The d20 roll you need, or more, to escape the worst of a poison, a spell or a dragon's breath.
